newsitem.title: USA: FINEX sets July 11 for Asian currency futures plan.
newsitem.headline: FINEX sets July 11 for Asian currency futures plan.

text.p: FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange (NYCE), now plans to launch its new Asian currency futures contracts on July 11, exchange officials said.
"We've now got a date - it's July 11 and we plan to launch contracts on the Indonesian rupiah, the Thai baht, the Malaysian ringgit," FINEX marketing director, Charles Minaar said.

"But we're still not quite sure about the date for the Singapore dollar, we're hoping we can do it on the same day, but we are still in discussions with the MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore)," he said.

Earlier in June the exchange said it planned to launch the currency products on June 26, but deferred the launch of its Asian currency products due to difficulties finalizing settlement issues with Asian authorities.
Both the Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Indonesian central bank have expressed concerns about the launch of the new products.
The currency pairs to be traded are: U.S. dollar/Indonesian rupiah, U.S. dollar/Thai baht, U.S. dollar/Malaysian ringgit and U.S. dollar/Singapore dollar.
